words.sense: Fair in relation to people’s needs, contributions, or circumstances.
misconceptions: Confused with equal when the defining clue is overlooked.

words.sense: The same in quantity or treatment, regardless of fairness.
misconceptions: Confused with equitable when the defining clue is overlooked.

semantic_axes.description: Equitable adjusts for relevant circumstances to achieve fairness; equal means giving or having the same amount.

edges.boundary_rule: Equitable adjusts for relevant circumstances to achieve fairness; equal means giving or having the same amount.
clues_a: Fair in relation to people’s needs, contributions, or circumstances.
clues_b: The same in quantity or treatment, regardless of fairness.
irrelevant_clues: format, colour, or popularity unless they establish the boundary
location or timing that does not change the decisive feature

misconceptions.M1: Treating equitable as though it always means equal.
misconceptions.M2: Treating equal as though it always means equitable.
misconceptions.M3: Overvaluing a distracting detail instead of the decisive semantic distinction.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Mariam’s distribution of tips?

beats.text: Mariam distributed tips according to hours worked, so longer shifts received larger shares.
beats.decisive_clue: shares reflected each volunteer’s actual contribution
beats.reason: This establishes that shares reflected each volunteer’s actual contribution.

beats.text: She counted the setup time that customers had not seen.
beats.decisive_clue: shares reflected each volunteer’s actual contribution
beats.reason: Counting unseen preparation supports a fair allocation rather than identical payouts.

chains.feedback_short: Shares reflected each volunteer’s actual contribution; that detail favors equitable.
chains.feedback_deep: Counting unseen preparation supports a fair allocation rather than identical payouts. Equitable adjusts for relevant circumstances to achieve fairness; equal means giving or having the same amount.
chains.contrast_rule: Equitable asks what is fair; equal asks what is the same.

hints.attention: Consider whether contributions affect the shares.

hints.contrast: Equitable asks what is fair; equal asks what is the same.
